name: Please, Please, Please Let Me Get What I Want

podcast.body: Released in 1984, this song perfectly captured a sense of profound sadness, making it suitable for moments of deep introspection. The Smiths fully embraced the Tweetpop aesthetic, incorporating venerable and often melancholic lyrics, confessional themes, jangly guitars, clear influences from 1960s girl groups, and occasionally childlike qualities in their music. "More seat in The Smiths with a song that went perfectly for those times when you were so sad you could only lie down on your bed and cry."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was released as a B-side to "William, It Was Really Nothing" in August 1984, alongside another track. Despite being initially relegated to B-side status and possibly considered "too radical" or "space filler," it unexpectedly grew in popularity to become one of The Smiths' biggest songs. "The biggest song the Smiths ever released, but it didn't start out that way. It was originally relegated to mere B side status."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Digital Debris Part 1: B-Sides and Bonus Tracks

podcast.body: Released in August 1984, this song is described as one minute and 50 seconds of naked emotion and unbearable sadness, considered by some to be the perfect Smiths song, while others found it very wimpy. "The Smiths from August 1984 and please, please, please, let me get what I want."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
